title: Preprocessing, clustering, and marker-based annotation of bone-marrow cells

sources.locator: Markdown headings Preprocessing and clustering; Quality Control; Normalization; Feature selection; Dimensionality Reduction; Nearest neighbor graph construction and visualization; Clustering; Re-assess quality control and cell filtering; Manual cell-type annotation; Differentially-expressed Genes as Markers; setup and code cells

scientific_use: Analyze two healthy-donor bone-marrow mononuclear-cell samples from 10x Multiome gene-expression data: compute QC metrics and doublet scores; filter cells/genes; normalize and log-transform counts; select highly variable genes; compute PCA, a neighbor graph, UMAP and Leiden clusters at several resolutions; inspect marker expression and rank cluster markers for manual cell-type annotation. The tutorial warns that cells are not independent biological replicates for differential expression and suggests sample-aware pseudobulk aggregation as a follow-up.
tool_role_basis: The notebook composes Scanpy and AnnData APIs (read_10x_h5, pp.calculate_qc_metrics, pp.scrublet, pp.normalize_total, pp.highly_variable_genes, tl.pca, pp.neighbors, tl.umap, tl.leiden, tl.rank_genes_groups) over external count matrices; it does not implement these algorithms.
inputs: Two 10x filtered feature-barcode HDF5 matrices, s1d1_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 and s1d3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5, loaded as AnnData and concatenated with a sample label; narrative reports about 8,000 cells per sample and 36,601 measured genes.
Counts are retained in adata.layers['counts']; downstream workflow uses normalized/log1p values and the count layer for some analyses.
outputs: AnnData with QC annotations, filtered cells/genes, count layer, highly-variable-gene flags, PCA, neighbors, UMAP, Leiden labels at multiple resolutions, marker-based manual cell_type_lvl1 annotation and differential-expression results in uns.
Figures illustrating QC, embeddings, cluster marker expression and ranked genes; figure export is shown.
dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, pooch; optional dependencies for Scrublet and Leiden implementation are environment-dependent and need pinning by task author.
Input files are resolved through Pooch DOI registry 10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1 and require network access unless staged.
Manual annotation relies on marker gene knowledge/resources; notebook marker list is adapted from Single Cell Best Practices annotation guidance.
Potential pseudobulk follow-up requires grouping counts by sample and cell type and an external differential-expression package such as PyDESeq2.
evidence: Tutorial narrative identifies healthy human donor bone-marrow mononuclear cells, OpenProblems NeurIPS 2021 data, 10x Multiome Gene Expression and Chromatin Accessibility, and approximate per-sample cell/gene counts.
Setup code declares Figshare DOI registry, filenames, read_10x_h5 and sample concatenation.
Workflow cells show filtering, Scrublet, count-layer preservation, normalization, HVGs, PCA, neighbors, UMAP, Leiden, manual labels, rank_genes_groups and rank_genes_groups_df.
Final discussion warns about cell-level p-values and suggests pseudobulk by sample/cell type.
limitations: Counts and notebook outputs were inspected as source only; no execution or result validation was performed.
The DOI landing metadata, individual file sizes, exact cell counts, and license/redistribution terms were not independently verified.
Manual annotation is partly subjective; task author must define expected label vocabulary and grading criteria.
The notebook uses two samples; inference/generalization beyond these samples is not established.
Need pin optional dependency versions and decide whether to supply raw files or pre-stage them.

title: Reference mapping and batch-aware neighbor graph integration

sources.locator: Headings Integrating data using ingest and BBKNN; PBMCs; Mapping PBMCs using ingest; Using BBKNN; Pancreas; BBKNN; Mapping onto a reference batch using ingest; Evaluating consistency; Visualizing distributions across batches; associated setup, mapping, comparison and evaluation cells

scientific_use: Compare asymmetric Scanpy ingest mapping with BBKNN graph integration. On PBMC reference/query data, train PCA, neighbors and UMAP on an annotated processed reference and transfer labels/embeddings to a query sharing genes; separately concatenate batches and use BBKNN. On a four-study human-pancreas collection, inspect batch effects, construct batch-balanced neighborhoods, map labels/embeddings from a reference batch, and assess consistency with cross-tabulations and batch-density visualizations. The tutorial states ingest leaves the expression matrix invariant and depends on the reference capturing relevant biological variation.
tool_role_basis: Tutorial code calls Scanpy tl.ingest and external.pp.bbknn with PCA/neighbors/UMAP plus AnnData concatenation and evaluation; it applies existing packages rather than implementing integration algorithms.
inputs: PBMC example: sc.datasets.pbmc3k_processed() as annotated reference and a query AnnData loaded by tutorial code; align common variables before reference PCA/neighbors.

Pancreas example: data/pancreas.h5ad, documented as already intersected on genes, downloaded from a Dropbox backup URL; observations have batch and celltype annotations, with multiple studies/batches.
For ingest, reference and query must share variables and the reference needs a fitted representation and graph; tutorial uses PCA, neighbors, UMAP and transferred louvain/celltype annotations.
outputs: Mapped query labels and PCA/UMAP coordinates under ingest while leaving query expression values unchanged.
BBKNN neighbor graph and downstream UMAP embedding on concatenated batches.
Consistency summaries using confusion/crosstab comparisons and embedding-density plots by batch.
dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, NumPy/pandas, plotting stack; BBKNN is provided through scanpy.external and requires its optional bbknn dependency.
Reference preprocessing and graph must be fitted before ingest; matching gene universe and consistent annotation columns are required.
Pancreas file is a separately curated combined asset; notebook links scGen notebook, BBKNN curation notebook and a BBKNN paper FTP archive.
evidence: Notebook narrative distinguishes asymmetric ingest from symmetric integration, explains shared variables and reference coverage, and notes matrix invariance.
PBMC code loads pbmc3k_processed reference, intersects variables and calls tl.ingest; later code concatenates and calls external.pp.bbknn.
Pancreas narrative names human pancreas and four cited studies (Segerstolpe2016, Baron2016, Wang2016, Muraro2016), and discusses batch effects, reference mapping and label-consistency evaluation.
Pancreas code reads data/pancreas.h5ad and supplies Dropbox backup URL; tutorial points to BBKNN curation and FTP paper archive.
limitations: Source file and linked archive were not downloaded or inspected; pancreas raw study accessions, exact study-to-batch mappings, metadata schema and licensing are unresolved.
The output labels and embeddings are context-dependent; grading must account for reference choice and expected mapping ambiguity.
No execution or claim of integration quality is established by source inspection.
Optional BBKNN dependency/version and exact PBMC query provenance should be resolved before task construction.

title: PAGA graph abstraction and pseudotime for mouse myeloid progenitors

scientific_use: Explore mouse myeloid progenitor differentiation using Scanpy's Paul et al. 2015 dataset. Preprocess with recipe_zheng17, build a graph and clustering, abstract cluster connectivity with PAGA, initialize a force-directed embedding from PAGA, choose a stem-cell root for diffusion pseudotime, and visualize selected gene changes along erythroid and myeloid paths.

Tutorial applies recipe_zheng17, PCA, neighbors, draw_graph, Louvain, PAGA, cluster annotation, a selected root in the stem cluster, and DPT.
Selected lineage paths and gene lists are manually specified in notebook code.
outputs: Annotated AnnData with preprocessing, neighborhood graph, clusters, PAGA connectivity abstraction, graph embedding, root-dependent dpt_pseudotime and figures of selected genes/path trends.
dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, numerical/scientific plotting dependencies; Louvain/igraph backend and drawing dependencies may need pinning.
The PAGA graph is built from a chosen clustering; DPT depends on the chosen root index, while lineage path/gene choices are supplied manually.
Source data are retrieved through Scanpy's dataset registry; raw and processed representations are used at different stages.

title: UMI quality control, Pearson-residual feature selection and clustering

sources.locator: Headings How to preprocess UMI count data with analytic Pearson residuals; Background; Download data; Load data; Perform Quality control; Use Pearson residuals for selection of highly variable genes; Transforming raw counts to Pearson residuals; Optional input arguments; chunksize; Wrapper functions; code cells for pbmc3k and pbmc10k_v3

scientific_use: Process two 10x PBMC UMI count matrices (3k v1 chemistry and 10k v3 chemistry) in parallel. Perform QC and filtering, select 2,000 highly variable genes using analytic Pearson residuals, transform the reduced raw-count matrices to residuals, then compute PCA, t-SNE, neighbors and Leiden clusters and compare cluster structure with known PBMC marker genes. The tutorial explains residuals as a variance-stabilized representation, describes theta and clipping options, and warns the residual matrix becomes dense, motivating gene selection and chunked computation first.
tool_role_basis: The notebook uses Scanpy experimental.pp highly_variable_genes and normalize_pearson_residuals plus standard pp/tl APIs on public 10x inputs; it does not implement Pearson residual or clustering algorithms.
inputs: 10x PBMC 3k v1 filtered gene-barcode matrix tarball (human hg19 path) and PBMC 10k v3 filtered feature-barcode matrix tarball; notebook gives exact URLs and SHA-256 hashes.
Sparse raw UMI counts; mitochondrial gene flag, cell/gene QC metrics and filtering thresholds are computed in notebook.
Marker genes adapted from PBMC3k tutorial provide a qualitative biological comparison.
outputs: Per-dataset highly_variable annotations and selected matrices; raw counts retained in layers['raw'] and depth-normalized square-root counts in layers['sqrt_norm'].
AnnData with dense analytic Pearson residual matrix, PCA, t-SNE, neighbor graph and Leiden clusters; comparison plots with marker-gene expression.
dependencies: Scanpy experimental API, AnnData, pooch, SciPy/scikit-learn plotting ecosystem; input tarballs are downloaded from 10x URLs unless staged.
Gene selection should precede residual transformation to limit dense-matrix memory; tutorial discusses chunksize and illustrates a separate 2-million-cell case requiring 500 GB RAM, not this example.
UMI count input and the tutorial's specified theta/clipping choices are material to reproducibility.
evidence: Tutorial narrative identifies two 10x datasets, their chemistries, links to 10x dataset pages and purpose of marker comparison.
Code provides exact tarball URLs, SHA-256 values, extraction paths and read_10x_mtx input directories.
Cells show QC, residual-based HVG selection, count-layer retention, residual conversion, PCA, neighbors, Leiden and marker plots.
Narrative documents dense residual memory implications, theta, clipping and chunking guidance.
limitations: The 10x page metadata and redistribution terms were not independently verified; source URLs and tutorial hashes are recorded as source claims.
No execution performed; dense residual memory and runtime depend on chosen data stage and environment.
Marker agreement is qualitative and is not a deterministic biological truth oracle.
The 3k source represents same observations as Scanpy PBMC3k dataset record but this tutorial's tarball is raw 10x matrix; linked processed H5AD is a distinct derived asset.

title: Score cell-cycle phases and regress cell-cycle effects in hematopoietic progenitors

sources.locator: Headings Cell-Cycle Scoring and Regression; Load data; Load cell cycle genes; Standard filters; log-transformation; cell cycle scoring; PCA on cell-cycle genes; regress S_score and G2M_score; post-regression PCA

scientific_use: On murine hematopoietic progenitor expression data, filter cells/genes, normalize and log-transform expression, score S and G2M phases from filtered human gene lists, visualize phase separation in PCA restricted to cell-cycle genes, regress both scores from the full expression matrix, then compare the PCA projection again. The notebook notes it uses the whole dataset rather than highly-variable genes because too few cell-cycle genes would otherwise remain for scoring.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial applies Scanpy preprocessing, tl.score_genes_cell_cycle, tl.pca and pp.regress_out to an input matrix and gene lists; it does not implement these methods.
inputs: Expression matrix from `nestorawa_forcellcycle_expressionMatrix.txt` within the Seurat tutorial ZIP, read as CSV/TSV and transposed into cells by genes.
Cell-cycle gene set from Tirosh et al. 2015, split into S and G2M lists and filtered to genes present in the matrix.
The included matrix is attributed by tutorial prose to murine hematopoietic progenitors from Nestorowa et al., Blood 2016.
outputs: AnnData with QC-filtered and normalized/log-transformed expression, S_score, G2M_score, phase annotations, and cell-cycle-score-regressed expression.
PCA projections restricted to cell-cycle genes before and after regression, colored by phase.
dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, pooch, pandas-like delimited text reader and PCA dependencies.
Tutorial ZIP must be staged/downloaded; source file path inside archive is named explicitly.
Human Tirosh cell-cycle gene symbols are intersected with observed feature names; using another organism requires appropriate ortholog mapping per tutorial.
evidence: Tutorial introduction names murine hematopoietic progenitors, Nestorowa et al. Blood 2016 DOI 10.1182/blood-2016-05-716480 and points to Seurat tutorial files.
Setup code gives Dropbox ZIP URL, SHA-256, and path of the expression matrix inside the archive.
Notebook describes 97 Tirosh cell-cycle genes split into S and G2M lists, filters, normalization, scoring, PCA, regression and post-regression PCA.

title: Compare exact and approximate neighbor transformers in a Paul15 workflow

This supports a task about choosing/configuring neighbor backends and assessing downstream graph/embedding effects.

outputs: Neighbor distances/connectivities for each backend, followed by Leiden labels and UMAP coordinates.
Notebook records timing comparisons and side-by-side plots; its stated comparison is qualitative.
dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, sklearn-ann, Annoy and PyNNDescent; notebook includes package install cells.
PCA is the default neighbor representation and is explicitly computed before comparisons.
The tutorial uses notebook timing magic; comparable performance claims require a pinned machine/software environment.

title: Measure graph autocorrelation for cell features or embeddings with Moran's I
source_kind: Public API operation and API documentation example

sources.locator: morans_i docstring and implementation, lines 27-109 verified against raw pinned file

scientific_use: Compute Moran's I global autocorrelation statistic over a cell graph for a scalar feature or multiple features such as PCA components. The documented example uses the default connectivities in a processed PBMC68k AnnData object and calculates one statistic per component; the public function also accepts an explicit graph and values from layers, obsm, obsp or raw expression.
tool_role_basis: This unit applies the public scanpy.metrics.morans_i operation to an existing neighbor graph and feature values; reading the implementation only confirmed semantics, not tool creation.
inputs: AnnData containing a graph (default neighbors connectivities or a selected graph) and values, or an explicit sparse graph plus a 1D cell vector or 2D features-by-cells array.
Documented example uses pbmc68k_processed() and adata.obsm['X_pca']; values are transposed from n_cells x n_features to n_features x n_cells by the AnnData API path.
outputs: Scalar for 1D values or 1D array of one global Moran's I value per feature for 2D values.
No mutation/output artifact is documented; caller must save or compare returned values.
dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, sparse graph representation and feature matrix; graph semantics/weights come from supplied AnnData or explicit graph.
The selected graph, feature slot, preprocessing stage and any missing-value handling must be specified by the author.
evidence: API docstring describes graph autocorrelation, accepted graph/value sources, shapes and scalar/vector return behavior.
Pinned API example computes Moran's I for each PCA component in sc.datasets.pbmc68k_processed() and compares to call on underlying arrays.
Public metrics API page lists metrics.morans_i.
limitations: The metric is global per feature and does not localize which cells drive autocorrelation.
Interpretation depends on graph construction, feature transformation and weights; the example uses precomputed graph/PCA inputs.
Only API documentation and source semantics were inspected; no execution or value verification was performed.
